### Step 1 — Scene
A breakfast/snack-style plate with bacon, sliced sausage, cooked potato chunks, grapes, and almonds.

### Step 2 — Vessel
A shallow dinner plate, approximately **26 cm diameter**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### Steps 3–6 — Items, area, volume, and weight
Food covers approximately **50%** of the plate. Heights represent the average outer envelope; bulk density is the only adjustment for gaps.

| Item | Plate area | Area (cm²) | Height (cm) | Gross volume (ml) | Density (g/ml) | Weight (g) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked bacon | 14% | 74 | 0.5 | 37 | 0.90 | 33 |
| Sliced cooked sausage | 9% | 48 | 1.8 | 86 | 0.95 | 82 |
| Cooked potato chunks | 10% | 53 | 2.1 | 111 | 0.65 | 72 |
| Grapes | 10% | 53 | 1.8 | 95 | 0.65 | 62 |
| Almonds | 7% | 37 | 1.1 | 41 | 0.60 | 25 |
| **Total** | **50%** | **265** | | **370** | | **274** |

No separate sauce or dressing is visible. Any cooking fat on the potatoes is included in their energy estimate.

### Step 7 — Energy
- Bacon: 33 g × 540 kcal/100 g ≈ **178 kcal**
- Sausage: 82 g × 310 kcal/100 g ≈ **254 kcal**
- Potatoes: 72 g × 130 kcal/100 g ≈ **94 kcal**
- Grapes: 62 g × 69 kcal/100 g ≈ **43 kcal**
- Almonds: 25 g × 579 kcal/100 g ≈ **145 kcal**

### Step 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **274 g and 714 kcal** is plausible for this partly covered plate. Bacon, sausage, and almonds contribute most of the energy despite their modest volume.
